subject: gov.policy
name: Digital governance framework
milestone: A restitution workshop on 29 and 30 July 2026 presented a ten-dimension maturity diagnostic
position_end: Instruments to be articulated named as the digital and data strategies, the AI strategy, the identity platform, the sovereign cloud, a certification authority and a cybersecurity agency; plus critical-infrastructure mapping, a minimum security baseline, reference data registries, a single digital identity, and no AI platform deployed without data quality, auditability and human supervision; the regulator's president stated on 2026-07-30 that the working groups had proposed a six-to-twelve-month timetable for the main actions, with an action matrix and a monitoring mechanism to follow
note: the chain spans five bodies, two of which are not established as operational

subject: gov.policy
name: Global defence doctrine
milestone: Unveiled 2026-08-20
position_end: A new national defence doctrine placing digital and informational sovereignty among its five pillars, alongside sovereign strategic thought, watch and anticipation capacity, African responses to regional crises and republican ethics
note: announced in a speech; no doctrinal text, implementing body or appropriation is held

subject: gov.policy
name: National data governance strategy
note: named by the minister on 2026-07-29 as an instrument the state already holds; no text, adoption date or adopting act is held

subject: gov.policy
name: National digital plan 2026-2030
milestone: The government announced operationalisation of a US$500m partner tranche after talks with two development financiers
position_end: A US$1.5bn envelope: US$1bn of treasury investment over five years plus US$500m of external partner support; no finalised published plan document is locatable
sources: 2026-02-20 DRC operationalises $500m partner tranche of PNN2 financing (World Bank, AFD)|2025-10-10 DR Congo launches National Digital Plan 2026-2030 (PNN2) and first AI strategy
note: a circulating US$8.7bn total could not be corroborated and was resolved against in July 2026; the US$1bn treasury half is an announcement, not an appropriation

subject: gov.policy
name: National strategy for mobile and broadband coverage
milestone: National Connectivity Strategy 2026-2035 unveiled 2026-08-13
position_end: A National Connectivity Strategy 2026-2035 built on a shared-infrastructure model led by a tower company, with subsidy agreements signed with the four mobile operators to extend service to 40 underserved localities covering about 258,000 people, and a target of 3,000 localities and 16 million people by 2030; the fund's own strategy pages publish the operative selection framework - a 100-point priority index weighting strategic class 30, coverage deficit 20, population density 15, public infrastructure 15, local economic potential 10 and technical-financial feasibility 10, with localities above 60 points classed for immediate deployment - alongside rules confining subsidy to sites where an operator demonstrates a negative return over four years and imposing national roaming between all operators on sites scoring above 70
note: the strategy text is not held and the subsidy amounts and the tower company are not stated; the scoring framework is now published but did not select the first 40 localities, which the fund describes as a preparatory phase of sites proposed by the operators themselves, ten from each of the four

subject: gov.policy
name: Reorganisation of the digital mandate in the 2026 finance law
milestone: Enacted 2025-12-29
position_start: One section titled posts, telecommunications and new technologies and another titled digital
position_end: The first renamed posts and telecommunications and the second renamed digital economy, with credits moving from FC 145.7bn to FC 55.1bn and from FC 60.6bn to FC 226.7bn
note: combined the two sections are almost flat as a share of the budget, so the rise is substantially a transfer of mandate rather than new money

subject: gov.policy
name: Sectoral digital economy policy 2026-2030
status: In development, validated and awaiting adoption
milestone: Presented and validated by government at a Kinshasa ceremony 2026-08-04
position_end: Validated and referred to the Council of Ministers for adoption, on axes covering infrastructure, digital transformation of the administration, the digital economy, innovation and start-ups, cybersecurity, and data governance; not published, not costed and not budgetable
note: the validators' conditions name exactly what is missing: reliable baseline data and a completed costing

subject: gov.policy
name: Strategy for the protection of the information space
milestone: Adopted by the Council of Ministers at its 97th session, 28 August 2026
position_start: No government-wide strategy on platform content held
position_end: A government-wide strategy against abusive content on social media and digital platforms, carrying an interministerial task force chaired by the communication ministry, a citizen alert mechanism, integration of media literacy into the curriculum, and a technical and legal review of the regulation of the sector
note: the strategy text is not held; what is held is the Council of Ministers own account of what it adopted

subject: gov.legislate
name: Bill on the identification of natural persons
milestone: Tabled at the National Assembly bureau 2026-06-12
position_end: Tabled; it would set one legal frame for identification data and its collection, processing, retention and protection, impose security and interoperability requirements and connect civil-registry, migration and health databases; no committee report or plenary date is held
note: it runs alongside rather than through the twenty-year identity concession, and nothing on file connects the two

subject: gov.legislate
name: Code du numérique
milestone: Prosecutors instructed to open Digital Code cases without a complaint, 2026-08-17
position_start: The framework law in force, its third book governing personal data, with no data-protection authority operational
position_end: The same law in force and now being enforced on the state's own initiative: the attorney general at the Court of Cassation instructed judicial police officers to open Digital Code cases proprio motu and forward them for summary hearing, and the audiovisual regulator's president is contemplating closing TikTok outright after the platform did not act on a request to block more than 2,000 accounts
note: also invoked in March 2026 as the instrument for prosecuting leaks of official documents; no data-protection authority is operational, so the enforcement running is criminal rather than regulatory

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital-sphere taxes, permits and sanctions regulations
milestone: New tariff and permit schedule analysed on publication, August 2026
position_end: A new schedule of taxes, permits and sanctions now governs the digital sphere; the base holds a legal analysis of it rather than the instrument itself, so the issuing authority, instrument number and entry-into-force date are not established
note: The capture is an excerpt opening mid-argument; the primary instrument is not held.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Interministerial order on digital-sector duties, taxes and fees
milestone: Ministry's own 8 August social-media statement confirms arrete 015 stays in force but fully exempts registered 'entreprenant' start-ups under Digital Code Article 384
position_end: A two-tier dollar schedule keyed to whether a provider is judged dominant: cloud services US$5,000 local and US$15,000 foreign in the first tier against US$2,500 and US$10,000 in the second; data-centre declaration from US$25,000 to US$100,000 by tier; one startup line at US$100. In force on signature 2026-07-20 under its article 5; a surseance announced by the finance ministry on 1 August 2026 and denied on 6 August 2026, neither position resting on a published government text; ministry's 8 August statement confirms registered 'entreprenant' start-ups are now fully exempt (not merely the US$100 line reported earlier), still with no gazetted order or amending text published
note: a non-tax revenue instrument collected by the revenue directorate rather than the tax administration; the finance ministry communique announcing the surseance is now held, the gazetted order is not, and no text withdrawing the surseance has been published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Joint subcontracting enforcement by two regulators
milestone: Agreed at the telecommunications regulator's headquarters 2026-07-22
position_end: A harmonised reading of the legal texts, joint inspection teams and enforcement of local-content subcontracting rules on large operators, with scope stated beyond telecoms to digital services and electronic commerce
note: no written protocol, order or joint communiqué is held; the account is a news report of the meeting

subject: gov.legislate
name: Ordonnances-lois organising statistical activity
milestone: Adopted by the Council of Ministers 2026-08-28
position_end: draft ordonnances-lois adopted by the Council of Ministers on 28 August 2026, presented as the country's first legislation on the subject and as adapting the legal and institutional framework

subject: gov.legislate
name: Satellite internet service-provider licence
milestone: Granted by regulator communiqué, reversing a March 2024 prohibition
position_end: Still licensed; the licence conditions, spectrum awards and any enforcement outcome are not established
note: the only telecom licensing decision in the base with a dated before and after; civil society welcomed it as a corrective to incumbent monopoly abuse

subject: gov.legislate
name: Social register decree
milestone: A draft decree adopted at the 53rd Council of Ministers 2025-07-25
position_start: A draft decree adopted in council
position_end: No promulgated decree number, signature date or publication held at 2026-08-06
note: twelve months in the same state: adoption in council is not promulgation

subject: gov.protect
name: Mobile network service in conflict-held eastern territories
milestone: Fizi Territory, Baraka included, off all mobile and internet service since 2026-07-03; press-freedom restoration call 2026-08-17
position_start: One territory centre off all networks from March 2025 because generator fuel could not reach tower sites
position_end: Fizi Territory including Baraka off calls, SMS and internet since 3 July 2026 and still cut more than six weeks later, amid fighting between the army and Twirwaneho rebels allied to the M23 and the Congo River Alliance; soldiers seized the Starlink kits of four community broadcasters on 8 July, telling journalists the equipment would be returned only when the war ended, and some outlets have suspended news bulletins
note: the seizures from broadcasters are an ordered act by soldiers, which the earlier record of this row could not say; no licensing or administrative decision for occupied territory is held

subject: gov.protect
name: National data protection authority
milestone: No decree defining its organisation and functioning found
position_start: Required by article 262 of the code; the decree never drafted or signed and the body non-operational
position_end: Still not created; the minister said in March 2026 that structuring a professional network precedes its creation, and it was named again in July as a link in the cybersecurity chain
sources: 2026-03-16-rdc-reseau-responsables-protection-des-donnees-wearetech|2024-08-07 RDC - government urged to operationalise the Data Protection Authority|2026-07-30-rdc-chaine-responsabilite-visible-cybersecurite
note: two years of the same finding, running alongside a twenty-year exclusive foreign concession over citizens' identity data

subject: gov.protect
name: National network of data protection officers
milestone: Launched by the digital economy ministry in Kinshasa 2026-03-12
position_end: A national network live, supported by two civil-society bodies and framed as alignment with the continental convention; the first concrete step under article 262 since 2023
note: it moves the enforcement gap without closing it: a professional network is not a supervisory authority with sanctioning powers

subject: gov.protect
name: Nationwide social-media restriction
milestone: A restriction observed from about 1 February 2025, with no authority acknowledging an order
position_start: The restriction had ended before the window opened and no acknowledged legal basis was ever stated
position_end: No further nationwide restriction recorded to 2026-08-06; the 2025 shutdown count for the country is attributed to the eastern conflict rather than to a national order
sources: 2025-02-03-acces-restreint-reseaux-sociaux-actualite|2026-03-01 Rising Repression Meets Global Resistance Internet Shutdowns in 2025
note: the source carries no governance subject tag, so a network restriction sits outside the governance view

subject: gov.protect
name: Prosecution of offences committed through social media
milestone: Prosecutor general instructed judicial police officers, August 2026
position_end: The prosecutor general at the court of cassation instructed judicial police officers to pursue offences committed through social media, asking that files be transmitted quickly so cases can be heard in flagrante delicto under the digital code, whose article 360 carries one to six months' penal servitude and a fine of 500,000 to 1,000,000 Congolese francs for initiating or relaying false information targeting a person; it extends the justice minister's March 2026 call to the prosecution services
note: no case count, charge or outcome under the article is on file

subject: gov.regional
name: African Telecommunications Union headquarters
status: Implemented, ratified with no move date stated
milestone: Return to Kinshasa ratified 2026-07-23 at the union's 7th Plenipotentiary Conference
position_start: Headquarters outside the country, with arrears outstanding
position_end: Return ratified after more than US.4m of arrears was paid; no date for the move is stated
note: the arrears figure and the account are the posts and telecommunications minister's, given marking a year in office; a bid for an ITU Administrative Council seat for 2027-2030 is pending

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional free-roaming resolution
milestone: A resolution adopted mandating effective implementation across Central Africa by 2026-06-30
position_end: The deadline has passed with no implementation, tariff or country-specific measure held

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional satellite data-residency framework
milestone: Recommended by an expert panel at the regional regulators' tenth ordinary session, hosted in Kinshasa
position_end: It would require non-geostationary providers to establish terrestrial gateways within the region's jurisdiction, meet obligations equivalent to traditional operators and keep citizens' data on the continent; a recommendation, not an adopted instrument
note: DR Congo is the host rather than the author, and the session dates are not stated in the source

subject: gov.standards
name: National classification regime for official documents
milestone: An information note presented to the 82nd Council of Ministers 2026-03-13
position_end: Four levels of classification with access limited to cleared agents, traceability of transmissions, reinforced archiving and a ban on sending sensitive documents over private messaging or unsecured platforms
note: tied by its own account to the security context in the east, and standing directly against the access-to-information bill

subject: gov.standards
name: Order to return units consumed without justification
milestone: Ordered 2026-08-27
position_end: the four mobile operators ordered by the posts and telecommunications minister to return units and megabytes consumed abnormally or unjustifiably by their subscribers

subject: gov.standards
name: Regulator network-monitoring platform
milestone: Equipment installed and inspected 2026-08-26
position_end: monitoring equipment acquired and installed, inspected by the posts and telecommunications minister on 26 August 2026, to trace service-quality failures

subject: gov.standards
name: Telecom and postal consumer complaint procedure
milestone: Redress channel pressed publicly 2026-08-30
position_end: the regulator's freephone complaints line back at the centre of a public redress debate, with a civil-society account of unexplained credit loss and a students' body demanding field evidence for the regulator's claims
note: the communiqué itself is not held; the regulator's site is script-rendered and exposes no document path

subject: gov.discourse
name: Media and communications regulators partnership
milestone: Memorandum of understanding signed after two days of work, 19-20 August 2026
position_end: The audiovisual and communications council and the press-freedom council have formalised an institutional partnership by memorandum; no work programme, joint power or first action under it is on file

subject: gov.discourse
name: Permanent state-industry consultation framework for the digital sector
milestone: Agreed at a working session between the digital economy minister and the sector network 2026-08-06
position_end: Agreed as a standing mechanism between the ministry and the Reseau des acteurs du numerique after the dispute over the digital-sector tariff; no constituting text, membership or meeting schedule stated
note: the agreement is reported from a communique carried by the state news agency; no founding text is held

subject: finance.budget
name: Audited outturn for the digital sections
note: the FY2024 accounts are audited and closed by an audit-court report and a settlement law, but neither document is obtainable, so no audited figure is established at section grain

subject: finance.budget
name: Digital economy section appropriation
milestone: The 2026 finance law enacted, renaming the section and fixing its domestic credits
position_start: FC 60,627,481,411 domestic for FY2025, revised, with no original appropriation published
position_end: FC 81,698,223,741 domestic for FY2026, appropriated
note: up 34.8% on FY2025 but still 6.2% below the FY2024 appropriation; on the export's own conversion the line has fallen in dollars

subject: finance.budget
name: Digital economy section expenditure chain
milestone: The budget ministry's year-end provisional situation closed the FY2025 chain
position_end: FC 31,358,784,468 paid, 51.7% of the revised credit, against FC 68,457,537,329 engaged, or 112.9%
note: the prior year's outturn is published by function and cannot be attributed; no credibility ratio is computable because FY2025 has no published original appropriation

subject: finance.budget
name: Financing of the finance inspectorate's digitalisation programme
milestone: Source of funds clarified 2026-08-26
position_end: the US$22m presented in May 2026 as already-identified financing confirmed as the state's own allocation rather than donor money

subject: finance.budget
name: FY2026 budget execution
note: the budget ministry had published nothing for the 2026 exercise seven months into the year

subject: finance.budget
name: National identification system appropriation
milestone: Appropriated inside the digital section's domestic investment group
position_end: FC 20,654,178 appropriated for FY2026
note: the figure cross-foots exactly against the group total and is not a transcription error; it corroborates the identification office's own statement that the allocation obliged recourse to a partnership

subject: finance.budget
name: Posts and telecommunications section appropriation
milestone: The 2026 finance law enacted, stripping new technologies from the section title and fixing its domestic credits
position_end: FC 53,840,917,417 domestic for FY2026, appropriated
note: partial scope: the externally financed investment group is excluded, so this is not the ministry's whole envelope

subject: finance.mou
name: Central bank card-network memorandum
milestone: A memorandum signed in Kinshasa by the central bank governor and a card-network executive
position_end: Three pillars: technical capacity building, financial inclusion and literacy, and secure resilient payment systems, aligned to the bank's 2026-2030 plan
note: no monetary value is attached and the signing date is not given separately from the report date

subject: finance.mou
name: Digital economy ministry memorandum with a commercial bank
position_end: Signed between the digital economy ministry and a commercial bank to modernise the financial ecosystem and accelerate banking inclusion, covering digital identity and artificial-intelligence integration under the 2019 national digital plan and the 2023 Digital Code
note: no term, value, workplan or data-protection provision is published for an arrangement that names digital identity as in scope

subject: finance.new
name: Eastcastle Debt II (IFC debt facility)
milestone: Reported at pipeline/identification stage 2026-07-16
position_end: US$34.35m IFC debt financing proposed for Eastcastle Infrastructure DRC to expand shared telecom tower infrastructure and mobile broadband capacity
note: A separate IFC facility from the EAAIF-financed US$179m senior facility to the same recipient (COD-finance.new-tower-platform-senior-facility); whether the two are linked is not established

subject: finance.new
name: Tower operator investment convention
milestone: An investment convention of more than US$100m signed with the investment-promotion agency
position_end: More than US$100m committed to extend connectivity in Kinshasa and the provinces, with more than 4,000 jobs stated as already created
note: the convention text is not held and no disbursement or drawdown figure is held

subject: finance.new
name: Tower platform senior facility
milestone: A development fund committed US$32.8m into an upsized US$179m senior secured facility
position_start: A US$30m commitment in 2023 supporting tower purchase and development, with the network at 1,072 active towers
position_end: US$32.8m inside a US$179m upsized facility funding 728 new passive towers to take the network to 1,800, 70% of them rural, plus solar and battery upgrades
note: the clearest staged facility in the country's finance record: same lender, same borrower, two dated positions three years apart

subject: finance.new
name: TRANSFORME Lobito corridor additional financing
milestone: Draft ratifying ordinance-law adopted by the Council of Ministers 2026-08-14
position_end: A US$200m IDA additional financing for extending the TRANSFORME enterprise project into the Lobito corridor, made up of a US$176m credit and a US$24m credit, its loan agreement concluded 22 June 2026 and its ratifying ordinance-law adopted in draft by the Council of Ministers. The parent project was approved in 2022 at US$300m, taking TRANSFORME to US$500m
note: adopted in draft; the ordinance-law is not yet promulgated and no disbursement is on record. The financier's own project paper of 5 June 2026 carries the project identifier P178176 and splits the US$200m into two credits; the two financing instruments signed on 22 June 2026 are separate disclosures and are not held

subject: infra.connect
name: 5G public consultation
milestone: The regulator opened a public consultation on introducing 5G
position_start: The consultation open since 2025-03-18 with no outcome published
position_end: Unchanged: no consultation report, spectrum award, licence or revised timetable seventeen months later
note: held only as an excerpt, because the communiqué is published as an image

subject: infra.connect
name: Africa Congo Internet Exchange
milestone: A second presence added at a Kinshasa carrier-neutral facility, making it the country's first distributed exchange
position_start: Established 2023 and operating from a single presence
position_end: A distributed exchange across two carrier-neutral facilities, open to licensed operators, service providers, mobile networks, cloud and content providers
note: no traffic, member-count or peering figure is held at either end

subject: infra.connect
name: DRC mobile subscription and internet-penetration statistics (EACO regional report)
milestone: EACO's first seven-country regulator-submitted dataset publishes ARPTC-sourced 2025 DRC figures
position_end: 73.93m mobile subscriptions, 67.8% penetration (from 63.96m/60.5% in 2024); 36.98m mobile-internet subscriptions, 33.9% penetration; mobile-internet revenue US$970.2m in 2025, nearly matching voice revenue; DRC reports no mobile-money transaction value to EACO

subject: infra.connect
name: Goma-Mombasa fibre route
milestone: The route reported lit, linking Goma to Mombasa via Kampala
position_end: Eastern DR Congo tied into the East African terrestrial corridor to the Indian Ocean
note: the event date is not separately established from the publication date, and both held accounts are trade press

subject: infra.connect
name: Kinshasa Internet Exchange (KINIX)
milestone: Exchange infrastructure relocated to a carrier-neutral Tier III facility 2026-08-20
position_end: The exchange moved its infrastructure into a carrier-neutral Tier III data centre in Kinshasa; the operators state it connects more than 20 networks with over 1 Tbps of available capacity and expect it to exceed 2 Tbps after the move. It is one of three exchange points under a national exchange project managed by the internet service providers association, and is positioned to become the primary national interconnection hub and a Central African regional exchange
note: capacity and network-count figures are the operators' own; no traffic measurement is held

subject: infra.connect
name: National digital transformation project fibre backbone
milestone: Deployment reported to the 95th ordinary Council meeting 2026-08-03
position_start: The programme running about a year with no deployed-kilometre figure held; the June 2025 Council recorded 30.79% mobile-internet and under 0.02% fixed access
position_end: 7,000 km deployed against a target of more than 18,500 km, leaving 11,500 km outstanding, tied to connecting 145 territories by 2030
note: the minister cites budget constraints and a low disbursement rate on external financing, attributed to donor procedure; the remaining distance over the 2030 horizon implies about 2,900 km a year

subject: infra.connect
name: Rural solar base-station joint venture
milestone: The commitment restated as 2,000 new solar-powered base stations by 2031
position_start: Announced January 2025: up to 2,000 solar 2G and 4G base stations over six years, reaching about 19m people
position_end: The same commitment restated sixteen months later with a 2031 date; no sites-built count, spend figure or first-phase milestone at either end
note: the base carries an announcement at both ends of the window and no delivery evidence in between

subject: infra.connect
name: Satellite direct-to-cell service
milestone: Commercial launch announced 2026-08-14
position_end: Commercially launched on 2026-08-14, the first African operator to move a satellite-to-mobile partnership out of testing; a compatible LTE Android handset with a clear view of the sky reaches messaging, SMS and voice by satellite where there is no terrestrial coverage, with no dish, router or other equipment, the regulator has confirmed a phased rollout, and eligible customers registering through the operator's app get a free 30-day introductory trial
note: the service is stated as designed for light data; a free 30-day trial is the only access term published — no standing tariff, coverage map or subscriber figure is on the record

subject: infra.connect
name: Sovereign satellite programme
milestone: The President received the promoter's representative, who said a bank had mobilised the estimated US$400m
position_start: A memorandum signed November 2024; cost estimated at US$400m and said to be mobilised
position_end: Unchanged: no contract, operator selection, build or launch date, and no revised cost on record in the following twelve months
note: the claim that a bank has mobilised the funds is relayed by the presidency, unnamed and uncorroborated

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink capacity in Kinshasa
milestone: Congestion notice to Kinshasa users, August 2026
position_end: Kinshasa users face four to six months of possible slowdowns while the network is congested; no subscriber count, capacity figure or remediation date is on file

subject: infra.connect
name: State telecommunications and postal operator
milestone: A directorate-general communiqué on the recovery setting out finances against staff grievances
position_start: A national conference on posts and telecoms named the sector the state's second-largest revenue source and asset spoliation a problem to fix
position_end: On current finances the company could theoretically pay salaries only every four months; management says rigour has brought the cycle to every two to two and a half months
note: a month-precision proxy date; no balance sheet, asset inventory or restructuring plan is held

subject: infra.store
name: Kinshasa carrier-neutral data centre
milestone: Certified to information-security, continuity and payment-card standards
position_start: Live since August 2024 as the country's first Tier III certified facility
position_end: The same certified position, now also hosting the internet exchange's second presence
note: certifications are not re-verified in the base and no recertification date is held

subject: infra.store
name: National data centre appropriation
milestone: The enacted 2026 finance law carries FC 26,756,546,346 for national data-centre acquisition
position_start: No national data-centre appropriation is established at the window's start
position_end: Appropriated in the enacted 2026 budget; no procurement, site, operator, specification or execution evidence is held
note: an appropriation is not a build, and no 2026 execution data has been published at all

subject: infra.store
name: Raxio group committed capital
milestone: Fresh equity lifted committed capital from US$350m to US$380m
position_end: US$380m committed capital, with six times as much power contracted in the first half of 2026 as in the first half of 2025
sources: 2026-07-15 Raxio data-centre capital tops $380m on investor boost
note: group-level across six live markets, with none of it allocated to DR Congo in the source

subject: infra.store
name: Raxio Kinshasa data centre
milestone: A contractor account of the delivered facility giving its build specification
position_start: Operating since August 2024 as the country's largest data centre
position_end: Tier III certified, 400 racks over 1,542 square metres, 1.5 MW, US$30m invested; no utilisation, capacity-sold or expansion figure is held
note: a wire source; the facility's position did not move in the window, only its parent's capital

subject: infra.store
name: Sovereign government cloud
milestone: Named by the digital economy minister among the projects to be ordered and made executable
position_end: Named as an existing ministry project alongside the digital and data strategies, the identity platform and a certification authority; no hosting location, operator, procurement, budget line or date is stated
note: the base carries no statement about a sovereign cloud before 2026-07-29, so its start position is unknown rather than zero

subject: infra.energy
name: Energy provision for digital infrastructure
note: six sources carry the tag and none names an energy instrument, programme or facility with a movable position; power appears only as a constraint inside connectivity items

subject: infra.capacity
name: National technical-capacity base
note: the wiki holds one source under this subject and it is a police cooperation accord; no named compute, high-performance computing, testing-laboratory or technical-institution object carries a position

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Child online-safety service
milestone: An operator launched the service at a Kinshasa press conference
position_end: A subscriber-level filtering service applying preset policies to a child's traffic, blocking adult, illegal, gambling and hate content and social platforms other than one messenger, from 50 units for 30 days
note: a commercial operator service rather than a state measure; no subscriber figure

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Functioning national incident-response capability
note: no dated position on a computer emergency response team, an incident-notification regime in operation, or a single recorded incident; the July 2026 workshop cites recent disruptions to public digital services that no held source names or dates

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cybersecurity agency
milestone: Named as one of five bodies whose roles in the incident-notification chain must be clarified, explicitly without creating new institutions
position_end: Named alongside a cybersecurity council, the data-protection authority, the central bank and the telecommunications regulator; whether the agency exists in law, is staffed or is operating is not established
note: the phrase without creating new institutions implies the agency is treated as already constituted, and no creating instrument, budget line or head is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Data-sharing platform and government payment gateway
milestone: Named as deliverables of the digital transformation project in the consultant tender
position_end: Specified on paper only: no architecture, pilot, operator or date, and the interoperability framework is itself a consultant deliverable
note: the minister's July 2026 common bases on a national architecture reference framework is the same object restated at ministerial level, still with nothing built

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National electronic certification authority
milestone: Named by the minister among the instruments to be articulated into the governance framework
position_end: Named, not established; a July 2026 interministerial order already prices qualified trust services at US$30,000 foreign and US$10,000 local
note: a fee schedule exists before the institution does

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Revenue-agency data cross-checking under systemic control
milestone: Named as the tax-base mechanism 2026-08-26
position_end: interconnection of the revenue agencies and a data warehouse named by the finance minister, on a first-year accountability broadcast, as the mechanisms meant to broaden the tax base
note: no platform, interface or timetable is named; the worked example given is a consignment imported at US$10,000 and declared to customs at US$1,000

subject: dpi.id
name: Biometric passport
status: Implemented, the supplier referred for trial
milestone: Fourteen defendants referred to trial, 31 August 2026
position_start: Produced under a supplier contract with no proceedings on record
position_end: The Belgian supplier that produced the passports from 2015 to 2025 referred to trial with thirteen others on charges of bribery of foreign public officials, money laundering and tax fraud, civil parties putting the diversion at close to US$60 million
